_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), series LKN3M SET-2, 31 pages. Page map (contact sheet, then every English page read at full size): idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, English on EVERY EVEN index 2-30, Hindi on every odd index 3-29; odd-page tops all open in Devanagari on the contact sheet; the last page idx 30 is English (Q39(a)(ii) and Q39(b)). Questions run 1-39 unbroken. Sections and per-question marks match sci80_2026 exactly: Section A Biology Q1-9 (1), Q10-12 (2), Q13-14 (3), Q15 case (4), Q16 (5); Section B Chemistry Q17-24 (1), Q25 (2), Q26-27 (3), Q28 case (4), Q29 (5); Section C Physics Q30-32 (1), Q33-34 (2), Q35-37 (3), Q38 case (4), Q39 (5). Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 2-10, every page footed {31/3/2}): OR in Q15 (whole branches), Q16, Q27, Q28 (c)(i)/(c)(ii), Q29, Q33, Q38 (c)(i)/(c)(ii), Q39 = 8 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. The scheme's other slashes (Q35(b) 'Alternate answer for (b)', Q13, Q29(b)(iv)) are alternative answers, not choices. MCQ keys read off the scheme image; no voids, grace notes or dual keys anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q38 table: 37·5). Sibling of 31/3/1: 38 rows copied byte for byte (stem, context, options, answer, chapter, subtopic, difficulty) after checking each on this paper's own page; 13 rows new. Q16's two alternatives are printed in the opposite order from 31/3/1 (the cyst drawing is (a) here). Q37 is NOT 31/3/1's Q35: this paper draws a myopic eye (31/3/1 a hypermetropic one) and words part (c) differently, so it was transcribed fresh.

questions.context: Not all plants carry out photosynthesis by the same mechanism. In most plants, it depends directly on gaseous carbon dioxide that diffuses into the leaf. However, some plants can store carbon dioxide in the vacuole of the leaf cells as part of a complex carbon compound. This compound is transported to the chloroplast and releases carbon dioxide when required for photosynthesis. This special mechanism is believed to have evolved as an adaptation in such plants which do not open stomata during the daytime to conserve water for survival in dry conditions (desert conditions).
